purpose: Independent practice of C1.2 — translating one given pattern rule into two additional representations (sound, body) while preserving the rule.
student_learning_goal: I can take one rule and show it as a parade of animals, sounds, and movements.

parts.answer_key: Sound parade: clap-stomp-stomp-clap-stomp-stomp (or any valid AB choice from the key, applied as ABB). Body parade: tall-small-small-tall-small-small. Both must follow the ABB rule consistently. Accept any reasonable representation that preserves the structural ABB rule using the icons in the key.

parts.part_title: Part 2: Which two have the SAME rule?
parts.student_instructions: Look at all three parades. Two of them follow the same rule. Circle the two that match. Write the rule on the line.

Each strip is ~5in wide with a thin black border surrounding it (so the student can circle the entire strip with one circle). To the right of each strip, a label: 'Animal parade', 'Sound parade', 'Body parade'. Below all three: 'The matching rule is: ____' with a writing line.

parts.answer_key: The student should circle the Animal parade AND the Sound parade. Both follow the AAB rule. The Body parade is ABB and does not match. The student should write 'AAB' on the line. A child who circles the matching pair AND writes the correct label has demonstrated abstraction past surface features — Level 3 on C1.2.

parts.answer_key: All three parades must follow the same rule the student wrote. Examples: Rule AB → animal Bea-Finn-Bea-Finn-Bea-Finn, sound clap-stomp-clap-stomp-clap-stomp, body tall-small-tall-small-tall-small. Rule ABB → animal Bea-Finn-Finn-Bea-Finn-Finn, sound clap-stomp-stomp-clap-stomp-stomp, body tall-small-small-tall-small-small. Correct if structural rule is preserved across all three rows.

early_finisher_prompt: If you finish, flip the page over and try to make a FOURTH version of your rule using SHAPES — circle and square. Could you also try numbers?
teacher_notes: Lesson 3 consolidation. This worksheet is the gate that confirms abstraction has landed (or not). Watch Part 2 carefully: a child who circles the wrong pair (e.g., circles all three) likely missed the AAB vs ABB distinction — flag for the standalone formative the next day. On Part 3, the third strip (body) is hardest because the body icons are less familiar than the animals. Accept stick-figure approximations. Use Part 2's circle and rule label as the most diagnostic data point — if it's wrong, the child needs the formative bridge before Lesson 4.
